title: Three-Way Tie at the Top: Águilas Sweep Guasave as the LMP First Half Races Toward Its Nov. 22 Finish
excerpt: The Águilas de Mexicali swept the league-leading Algodoneros de Guasave over the weekend, leaving Mexicali, Hermosillo and Guasave tied at 17-12 with one week left in the first half of the Liga Mexicana del Pacífico season.
content:
The race at the top of the Liga Mexicana del Pacífico is now a three-way tie. The Águilas de Mexicali swept the league-leading Algodoneros de Guasave in their ninth series of the 2026-27 season, winning 4-2 on Friday, 6-2 on Saturday and 10-1 on Sunday in Guasave, and the sweep pulled Mexicali level with Guasave and the Naranjeros de Hermosillo at 17-12.

Moisés Gutiérrez drove in the go-ahead runs in Friday's 4-2 win with a two-run home run, his fifth of the season. On Saturday, Yadir Drake hit a three-run home run and Gutiérrez added another solo shot in a 6-2 win backed by a strong start from Humberto Castellanos. Sunday was a rout: Mexicali scored two in the first, one in the second, two in the sixth and five in the seventh for a 10-1 win that completed the sweep.

Hermosillo kept pace by taking its series from the Charros de Jalisco, two games to one. The Naranjeros won 4-1 on Friday behind home runs from Nick Solak and César Salazar, dropped Saturday's game 8-1 as Jalisco hit three home runs, then closed out the series 4-2 on Sunday with RBIs from Luis González, Rubén Ibarra, Reivaj García and Solak. Rolando Mora earned his third win of the season with five and two-thirds innings of one-run ball.

The Tomateros de Culiacán, one game back at 16-13, opened their series against the Venados de Mazatlán with a 16-1 blowout on Friday. Manny Barreda worked five scoreless innings for his second win of the season while Culiacán hit four home runs and scored seven runs in the first inning alone. The Tomateros followed with a 14-5 win on Saturday, powered by a Fernando Flores grand slam in the eighth inning and a three-run home run from Luis Verdugo. Mazatlán avoided the sweep on Sunday, winning 4-1 behind Ernesto Borges, who allowed one run on one hit with six strikeouts over five innings for his first win of the year.

The Cañeros de Los Mochis were the weekend's other big winners, sweeping the Mayos de Navojoa for their third straight series win and second straight sweep. Los Mochis won 5-3 on Friday, 9-0 on Saturday and 9-8 in extra innings on Sunday, running their winning streak to five games. The Jaguares de Nayarit also won their fifth straight series, taking two of three from the Yaquis de Ciudad Obregón after dropping Friday's opener 6-2. Chávez Young hit a three-run home run in Saturday's 6-1 win, and Nayarit closed the series with an 8-4 victory on Sunday.

The first half of the season ends Sunday, Nov. 22, with points awarded by final position, so the final week carries real weight in the playoff race. The tenth series starts Tuesday, Nov. 17: Yaquis visit Cañeros, Tomateros host Jaguares, Naranjeros host Águilas in a first-place showdown, Algodoneros host Mayos and Charros host Venados.

Sources: Revista Deportemas (SANBUS wire), Nov. 13-16, 2026; Lado.mx, Nov. 15-16, 2026; Beis360 standings, Nov. 16, 2026; RCATimes, Nov. 14-15, 2026.
